headline: 61 days in a cell: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed recalls his enforced disappearance
summary: Speaking at an event by 'Mayer Dak', the Minister detailed the harrowing experience of being held in an 8x4 foot room with no medical care for his heart condition.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed shared his emotional account of being forcibly disappeared for 61 days in 2015 during the previous government's tenure.
He described being held in a tiny 8x4 foot room with only a blanket on the floor for bedding and a small hole for sanitation, which he said emitted a foul smell.
The Minister stated that he was given one breakfast and two meals a day, but despite having a heart condition, he was denied access to any medical treatment while in captivity.
He recalled theว่า an electric fan outside his door was his only source of air, stating that without it, he felt he would have suffocated within hours.
After 61 days, he was blindfolded and transported in several vehicles, including a microbus and a jeep, before being abandoned in a remote area of Shillong, India.
He described how local people in Shillong initially thought he was mentally unstable due to his state, before he was eventually rescued by the Indian police.
The Minister expressed that during his captivity, he feared he would die in a foreign land and that his family would never find his grave.
The event was organized by 'Mayer Dak', an organization of families of disappeared persons, to mark the International Day of the Prevalence of Enforced Disappearances.

An 8x4 foot room, no medical care for a heart condition, and 61 days of isolation. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reveals the trauma of his own enforced disappearance.

He described being held in a tiny 8x4 foot room with only a blanket on the floor for bedding and a small hole for sanitation, which he said emitted a foul smell.

After 61 days, he was blindfolded and transported in several vehicles, including a microbus and a jeep, before being abandoned in a remote area of Shillong, India.

He described how local people in Shillong initially thought he was mentally unstable due to his state, before he was eventually rescued by the Indian police.

The Minister expressed that during his captivity, he feared he would die in a foreign land and that his family would never find his grave.

The event was organized by 'Mayer Dak', an organization of families of disappeared persons, to mark the International Day of the Prevalence of Enforced Disappearances.

headline_marked: 17 districts including Dhaka: [[Thunderstorms and gusty winds forecast]]
headline: 17 districts including Dhaka: Thunderstorms and gusty winds forecast
summary: The Meteorological Department has issued a warning for 17 districts, predicting winds up to 60 kmph and potential thunderstorms.
details: The Meteorological Department has warned that gusty winds blowing at speeds of 45 to 60 kmph may occur in 17 districts across the country, including Dhaka, by morning.
The warning, issued on Saturday night, also predicts the possibility of rain or thunderstorms accompanying these strong winds.
The affected regions include Rangpur, Rajshahi, Pabna, Bobugra, Kushtia, Dhaka, Faridpur, Tangail, Mymensingh, Khulna, Barishal, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Comilla, Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, and Sylhet.
As a result, river ports in these areas have been advised to hoist signal number one from Saturday 8:30 PM to Sunday 9:00 AM.
